additional_info.subject: Additional description:
additional_info.body:
I went to the Napier charger yesterday and monitored the debug output from the vehicle side EVCC on the truck and on our test car. I found that the charge gun (gun 3 - the side that they use for the truck) is doing similar things to the one in Auckland that had issues.
Sometimes the charger limits the power (log 1 where we are requesting 50A and getting only 37A)
Sometimes the charger randomly stops the charging session (log 2 where we see a session starting, current flowing and then a message "EVSE Request to Stop")
Please investigate the reason for the low power session and stop charging command by the charger
*********PLEASE DO NOT UPGRADE FIRMWARE AS WE HAVE LOCAL ISSUES WITH SOME VERSIONS CAUSING THE CHARGER TO DROP OFF SCB*******
software version
: v4

additional_info.subject: ID0471840-DC/Si-D/NZ-[MP / P3 170000342]Power limited charging sessions CRM:02681001313
additional_info.body:
Dear Liz,
Thank you for reaching eMobility Support regarding the recent limited charging session and your observations about a potential issue with either the truck or the cable.
After reviewing the logs for a charging session on January 28th, we can confirm that we are indeed seeing an issue consistent with your report.
Our analysis shows frequent and repeated fluctuations in the insulation resistance throughout the charging period. These continuous fluctuations indicate an
underlying intermittent instability within the charging connection.
The charging session was ultimately terminated unexpectedly by the truck (EV) itself. This suggests that the truck's internal systems, likely reacting to the persistent instability caused by the fluctuating insulation resistance, decided to end the session prematurely.
This intermittent instability could be related to:
The charging cable:
Minor degradation or a connection issue.
The truck's charging inlet/system:
An issue within the vehicle's charging port or its internal high-voltage system.
To identify the root cause, we recommend the following:
For the truck's charging inlet/system:
Please have your maintenance team perform a thorough inspection of the truck's charging inlet and its internal high-voltage system for any signs of wear, damage, or loose connections.
For the charging cable:
A detailed inspection of the charging cable would require a Siemens technician on-site.
Please let us know if you would like to proceed with scheduling a cable inspection.
Please note that as your charger is outside of its warranty period, our policy allows for up to one hour of support, which has now been fully provided.
Best regards,
Ivan
Siemens eMobility Technical Support Team
